headline: Discussed syringe litter report and heard public comment on syringe service programs
summary: The committee held a public forum where residents gave mixed views on syringe service programs, citing both neighborhood concerns and public health benefits. The committee then discussed recommendations from a syringe litter report, including a citywide harm reduction definition and disposal notices, and planned to continue the discussion later.

3. Public Forum  
CITY OF BURLINGTON, VERMONT 
CITY COUNCIL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & 
NEIGHBORHOOD REVITALIZATION COMMITTEE 
c/o Community & Economic Development Office 
City Hall, Room 32 • 149 Church Street • Burlington, VT 05401 
802-865-7144 VOX • 802-865-7024 FAX • www.burlingtonvt.gov/cedo
• Amy Kimmel, Robert Perry, Ed Baker, Selena Colburn, Chris McGrath, 
Bella Fearn, Melo Grant, John Fletcher spoke during public forum  
• Community members expressed concerns about the impact of 
syringe service programs (SSPs) on neighborhoods, citing issues such 
as increased drug activity and syringe litter. Others, including 
representatives from Vermont Cares and harm reduction advocates, 
spoke in support of SSPs, emphasizing their public health benefits 
and the need for a community-wide approach to harm reduction 
 
4. Revisiting Syringe Litter Report 
• CDNR Committee members discussed the first recommendation, 
which proposed adopting a citywide definition of harm reduction 
principles, with counselors debating its practical implications and the 
need for a diverse stakeholder group to define it. The second 
recommendation, regarding notices for safe syringe disposal, was 
also discussed, with Vermont Cares confirming that they already 
provide education on proper disposal. The meeting adjourned with 
plans to continue the discussion on the remaining recommendations 
at a future date. 
 
5. Adjournment   
• ADJOURN at 8:11 p.m. by Councilor Schachter with no objection
